$comment: Pinned upstream snapshots. `uat vendor sync` fetches these commits verbatim;
`uat vendor verify` re-hashes the result so a hand-edited snapshot fails loudly.
POLICY: content under vendor/ is never edited. Our own policy lives in
catalog/core/ and catalog/packs/. If an upstream is wrong, add an overlay
pack rather than patching the snapshot.
LICENSING: only redistributable licences are vendored here. Figma's skills are
governed by the Figma Developer Terms rather than an OSS licence, so they are
NOT vendored - the figma pack ships our own integration guide and tells you to
install Figma's official skills from source yourself.

upstreams.notes: Jesse Vincent's engineering-discipline skills: brainstorming, writing-plans, TDD, systematic debugging, verification. The backbone of the planning workflow.
Vercel Labs interface quality checklist (accessibility, motion, forms, focus). AGENTS.md is the guideline text itself.

upstreams.notes: React and Next.js best practices from Vercel Labs. Deployment-specific skills are deliberately excluded.

upstreams.notes: Behavioural guardrails against LLM overcomplication: surgical changes, surfaced assumptions, verifiable success criteria.
GitHub's curated instruction library - 193 technology guides. The primary source of stack rules. Only the instructions/ directory is vendored; the full repository is ~200 MB.

Community rule collection (public domain). Quality varies and some entries are stylistic preference rather than best practice - used to fill gaps awesome-copilot does not cover. Review a rule before adding a pack for it.

UI/UX reference data: style catalogues, colour palettes, font pairings, UX guidelines. The 'ui-styling' (5.7 MB) and 'design' skills are excluded for size and API-key reasons - add them here if you want them.

not_vendored.reason: Governed by the Figma Developer Terms, not an OSS licence. Redistribution inside this repository is not clearly permitted.
not_vendored.how_to_get: The figma-design pack explains how to install Figma's official skills directly from source into your own project.
